soil-env-174.q: Under what conditions need inorganic fertilizers not harm soil health?
soil-env-174.a: When they are not used in excess and they boost plant growth that returns more carbon-containing residues.

soil-found-092.q: What is the familiar vernacular distinction between soils, and what makes light soils easier to cultivate?
soil-found-092.a: Heavy (clayey) versus light (sandy) soils. Light soils are easier to cultivate and resist compaction by trampling cattle, but they erode more easily.

soil-found-088.q: Why do tropical soils turn rusty red and lack marked layer contrasts?
soil-found-088.a: Fast decomposition leaves little fulvic acid to leach metals, so mobile magnesium, iron and aluminium precipitate as oxide minerals that colour the soil rusty red.

soil-found-079.q: Why is soil water more accurately called the soil solution?
soil-found-079.a: Because it is never pure: it carries hundreds of dissolved organic and mineral substances.

soil-found-042.q: How are clay minerals most easily identified?
soil-found-042.a: By X-ray diffraction rather than by chemical or physical tests.

soil-form-136.q: What is the minimum share of silt- and clay-sized particles in a mudrock?

soil-form-111.q: How do luminescence methods date loess?
soil-form-111.a: They date when the grains were last exposed to daylight.

soil-form-152.q: What happens when volcanic ash is washed into the soil, and when is heavy ashfall harmful?
soil-form-152.a: Its minerals form a nutrient-rich andisol layer that is very good for farming. Heavy ashfalls can bury pasture and sterilize the soil by oxygen deprivation.

soil-form-092.q: How do inflowing rivers sort sediment in a lake?
soil-form-092.a: They drop larger rocks and stones near the lake edge, while suspended sediment settles across the whole lake bed.

soil-form-154.q: What is rock varnish made of, and how does its clay arrive?
soil-form-154.a: It is made mainly of clay with iron and manganese oxides, and the clay can only arrive by wind.

soil-form-021.q: How is the depth of topsoil measured, and what horizons does it correspond to?
soil-form-021.a: From the surface to the first densely packed layer, the subsoil; classification systems call it the O or A horizon.

soil-form-022.q: Does the United States have a legal definition of topsoil sold in commerce?
soil-form-022.a: No, it has no federal legal definition.

soil-form-026.q: Why can a perched water table form on top of a claypan?
soil-form-026.a: Its dense structure restricts roots and water infiltration.

soil-form-040.q: Why does caliche form in the B horizon under a thin A horizon?
soil-form-040.a: Calcite and other soluble minerals that water would normally remove build up there as a cemented layer.

soil-form-035.q: Why are tepetates a problem for farming at the surface?
soil-form-035.a: They are hard, poorly drained and infertile.

soil-form-123.q: What kind of soils show this wetting-drying mixing, and what does it require?
soil-form-123.a: It is specific to vertisolic soils, driven by wetting-drying cycles, and needs at least 30% clay.

soil-form-158.q: How does humus change as a soil ages from young to old?
soil-form-158.a: In a young soil humus accumulates; in a mature soil it peaks; in an old soil it declines.

soil-form-156.q: Which part of a hillslope is steepest, and what shapes it?
soil-form-156.a: The backslope, shaped mainly by mass wasting and running water.

soil-form-167.q: What made the St. Lawrence Lowlands clays unstable after glaciation?
soil-form-167.a: The Champlain Sea left salt-rich clay there, and leaching of the salt plus river incision made it unstable, causing landslides and earthflows.

soil-form-164.q: What separates the great groups of the Chernozemic order?
soil-form-164.a: The colour of the A horizon, which shows how much organic carbon the grasses added.

soil-phys-052.q: What law is used to calculate particle size from terminal settling velocities?

soil-phys-186.q: How did agrophysics develop from soil physics?
soil-phys-186.a: It first studied relations within the soil, then widened to crop properties and the quality and safety of food and raw farm produce.

soil-phys-167.q: What did Coulomb contribute to soil design in 1773?
soil-phys-167.a: He applied mechanics to earth pressures on ramparts, taking shear strength on a slip plane as cohesion plus friction.

soil-phys-094.q: What do relative densities of 100% and 0% mean?
soil-phys-094.a: 100% means very dense sand or gravel; 0% means extremely loose, unstable soil.

soil-phys-067.q: How do IUPAC pore size limits relate to how gases adsorb on rigid solids?
soil-phys-067.a: Micropores fill cooperatively, mesopores show capillary condensation, and in macropores confinement effects vanish.

soil-phys-066.q: What is the difference between primary and secondary porosity?
soil-phys-066.a: Primary porosity is the original pore system of a rock or alluvial deposit; secondary porosity forms later, through leaching of minerals or fracturing.

soil-phys-087.q: Why are wet, clay-rich soils more susceptible to compaction?
soil-phys-087.a: Water films shield particle contacts, and fine-textured clay-rich soils are more susceptible than coarse ones, wet more than dry.

soil-phys-229.q: Why can freshly plowed soil falsely look uncompacted?

soil-phys-232.q: Why does a field headland usually yield less?
soil-phys-232.a: It gets more traffic per unit area than the rest of the field, so its soil is more compacted.

soil-phys-235.q: Why may switching compacted soil to no-till at once fail?
soil-phys-235.a: Compacted soils become addicted to tillage, and no-till benefits usually take 2 to 5 years, faster with cover crops.

soil-water-182.q: Why is Richards' equation hard to use for infiltration?
soil-water-182.a: It is computationally expensive, not guaranteed to converge, and sometimes struggles to conserve mass.

soil-water-198.q: How is horizontal saturated hydraulic conductivity measured with the auger hole method?
soil-water-198.a: A hole is augered to below the water table, water is bailed out, and the rate at which the level rises again is recorded.

soil-phys-130.q: What does a root do when it senses dry soil?
soil-phys-130.a: It makes the hormone ABA, which closes stomata, cutting transpiration and photosynthesis, and loosens root cell walls so roots grow in search of water.

soil-water-167.q: How is gravimetric water content found by oven drying?
soil-water-167.a: The sample is dried and weighed until drying is complete; the mass lost is the water, divided by the wet or the dry mass.

soil-water-242.q: What turns plinthite irreversibly into ironstone hardpan?
soil-water-242.a: Repeated wetting and drying, especially with heat from the sun; a single cycle does not.

soil-water-190.a: The ratio of actual path length to the straight distance between two points; the more sinuous the path, the higher it is.

soil-phys-255.q: What is the premise of pedotransfer functions?
soil-phys-255.a: That a soil's basic properties are enough to infer all its other physical and chemical properties.

soil-water-020.q: Why can Horton overland flow erode soil extensively?
soil-water-020.a: The flow is shallow, sheetlike and fast, especially on steep terrain and loose, flat farmland.

soil-phys-262.q: Between which two points is plant available water held?
soil-phys-262.a: Between field capacity and the permanent wilting point, in mesopores.

soil-water-211.q: Why does ponded water reach groundwater more readily than evenly spread rain?
soil-water-211.a: Rain spread evenly within field capacity barely percolates, but pooled in low spots the same volume can exceed field capacity and drain down to groundwater.

soil-phys-208.q: Which equation is the basic constitutive law for groundwater discharge, and who derived it?
soil-phys-208.a: Darcy's law, derived by Henry Darcy in 1856.

soil-phys-206.q: Where does subsurface water return to the surface?
soil-phys-206.a: At lower elevations through springs, seeps, wells or streams, sometimes after thousands of years in an aquifer.

soil-water-158.q: How is fingering in the unsaturated zone described?
soil-water-158.a: As a Saffman-Taylor instability, arising mostly during drainage and leaving an unstable boundary between saturated and unsaturated soil.

soil-water-165.q: At what suction is field capacity defined, and what moisture does it represent?
soil-water-165.a: At -33 kPa; it is the moisture 2-3 days after rain or irrigation.

soil-water-162.q: What does a general basin water balance say?
soil-water-162.a: P = Q + ET + change in storage: precipitation equals streamflow plus evapotranspiration plus change in storage in soil or groundwater.

soil-phys-211.q: What reservoirs does this water balance model divide the soil profile into?
soil-phys-211.a: The surface, the unsaturated root zone with mainly vertical flow, a transition zone, and the aquifer with mainly horizontal flow.

soil-phys-219.q: What does the eddy covariance flux measure, and what is it the covariance of?
soil-phys-219.a: It is the covariance between fluctuations of vertical wind speed and of gas concentration, times mean air density.

soil-phys-213.q: How much of the water roots take up is lost by transpiration and guttation?
soil-phys-213.a: 97-99.5%; only a small part is used for growth.

soil-phys-146.q: Why does soil air hold less oxygen and more CO2 than the air above?
soil-phys-146.a: Microbes and roots consume oxygen and release carbon dioxide.

soil-phys-150.q: What commonly causes poor soil aeration?
soil-phys-150.a: Soil compaction, and a pore network blocked when water fills the pores.

soil-phys-163.q: What drives the formation of patterned ground?
soil-phys-163.a: Frost heaving of wet, fine-grained, porous soils: repeated freezing and thawing push larger stones up, and lateral forces pile them into clusters and stripes.

soil-phys-161.q: What do low-albedo and high-albedo surfaces do with radiation?
soil-phys-161.a: Low-albedo surfaces look dark and absorb most radiation; high-albedo surfaces such as snow look bright and reflect most of it.

soil-phys-244.q: What does Dalton's law say about a gas mixture?
soil-phys-244.a: The total pressure of an ideal gas mixture is the sum of the partial pressures of its gases.

soil-phys-245.a: Without convection, gases are good insulators, so they trap many gas-filled pockets that block conduction.

soil-phys-179.q: What conditions does ice segregation need?
soil-phys-179.a: A permeable soil or porous rock, temperatures at which ice and premelted water coexist, and a temperature gradient across the zone.

soil-phys-164.q: What is the formula for thermal diffusivity, and what does high diffusivity mean?
soil-phys-164.a: alpha = k/(rho cp). Heat moves rapidly through a material of high diffusivity because it conducts heat quickly relative to how much energy it stores.

soil-phys-183.q: What does the heat equation say about how a point heats or cools?
soil-phys-183.a: A point heats or cools at a rate proportional to how much hotter or cooler its surroundings are.

soil-chem-231.q: Why does anatase often form first even though rutile is more stable?
soil-chem-231.a: Anatase has a lower surface energy, though rutile is the most common and stable TiO2 polymorph.

soil-chem-232.q: Why does each element give its own X-ray emission peaks?
soil-chem-232.a: An incident beam ejects an inner-shell electron, and the X-ray released when an outer electron fills the hole has an energy characteristic of the element.

soil-chem-188.q: What does Bragg's law link together?
soil-chem-188.a: The wavelength, the lattice spacing and the glancing angle.

soil-chem-233.q: What gives this phosphate mineral its green colour?

soil-chem-242.q: What happens when pyrite is exposed to air?
soil-chem-242.a: It oxidizes to iron and sulfuric acid, and oxidation of sulfides can push soil pH below 2.0.

soil-chem-108.q: What conditions does bauxite formation need?
soil-chem-108.a: Intense weathering and very good drainage, which dissolve kaolinite and precipitate gibbsite.

soil-chem-227.q: How does the van der Waals force change with distance?
soil-chem-227.a: It is repulsive at very short range, zero at an equilibrium distance, and attractive beyond it.

soil-chem-109.q: Where does green rust occur as a mineral?
soil-chem-109.a: As the mineral fougerite in Gleysols.

soil-chem-089.q: What alternating conditions helped kaolinite form on basalt in Kivu?
soil-chem-089.a: Alternating wet and dry seasons; it did not form in perennially swampy ground.

soil-chem-148.q: How many milliequivalents is 1 mmol of Ca2+?
soil-chem-148.a: 2, because the equivalents of an ion equal its moles multiplied by its valence (1 mmol of Na+ is 1).

soil-chem-054.q: Does base-richness predict nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium availability?
soil-chem-054.a: No: base-richness shows no correlation with their availability.

soil-chem-115.q: What is the main source of electrons in soil?

soil-chem-229.q: Why do particles sometimes stay suspended as a colloid instead of settling?
soil-chem-229.a: There is not enough attractive force to aggregate them.

soil-chem-173.q: What role does manganese play in plants?
soil-chem-173.a: It is a key micronutrient, acting as a catalyst in the oxygen-evolving complex of photosystem II.

soil-chem-041.q: Why can both over-irrigation and under-irrigation cause salinity?
soil-chem-041.a: Over-irrigation raises water tables; under-irrigation fails to flush out salts.

soil-chem-040.q: Which equation does this model numerically solve to compute groundwater levels and flows between polygons?

soil-chem-042.q: How does framboidal pyrite form in acid sulfate soils?
soil-chem-042.a: Bacteria such as Desulfovibrio desulfuricans reduce sulfate to hydrogen sulfide, which reacts with ferrous iron.

soil-chem-220.q: What is the only way to remove salt from soil, rather than just tolerate it?
soil-chem-220.a: Washing salt below the root zone.

soil-bio-008.q: What is the primary role of soil biota?
soil-bio-008.a: To recycle organic matter that comes from the above-ground, plant-based food web.

soil-bio-271.q: Why does the hyphal form suit fungi?
soil-bio-271.a: Its high surface-to-volume ratio suits nutrient extraction and invading substrates.

soil-bio-056.q: What do lithotrophs get their name from?
soil-bio-056.a: The Greek lithos (rock) and troph (consumer): they are 'eaters of rock'.

soil-bio-017.q: Why are slime molds not found far below the surface?
soil-bio-017.a: They need light, so they are spread wherever sunlight and moderate moisture reach.

soil-bio-274.q: How are protozoa classified by how they move?

soil-bio-083.q: How do entomopathogenic nematodes kill an insect?
soil-bio-083.a: An infective juvenile enters it and releases gut bacteria, Xenorhabdus or Photorhabdus, that kill it within 24-48 hours.

soil-bio-064.q: What distinguishes biologically controlled mineralization from induced mineralization?
soil-bio-064.a: In controlled mineralization the cells of one organism fully control the crystals' shape, growth, composition and location; in induced mineralization microbial metabolism merely creates conditions that favour mineral growth.

soil-bio-211.q: Why are millipedes called soil ecosystem engineers?
soil-bio-211.a: Their burrowing mixes organic with mineral matter, especially where earthworms are absent or scarce.

soil-bio-006.q: What are root tips hotspots of?

soil-bio-031.q: How does a Baermann funnel collect nematodes?
soil-bio-031.a: Nematodes sink into the collecting vial because they cannot swim.

soil-bio-221.q: How does metagenomics differ from amplicon sequencing?
soil-bio-221.a: Amplicon sequencing of marker genes such as 16S rRNA shows which taxa are present; metagenomics sequences all DNA and also recovers enzymes and pathways.

soil-bio-273.a: Organisms that parasitise fungi are called mycoparasitic.
